posts.name: EvanDan55
posts.cooked:
Really? We actually find the tokens pretty useful. The problem we had back when using D10s was just running out of them; I only have 18 D10s. I love these tokens. It really doesn't take too long to subtract from the heroes HP, and for the villain, we find it easier to just count up with tokens rather than giving them their full HP and subtracting. It doesn't take but a second to do a villain 2 damage, and throw 2 tokens on him. Then whoever is running the villain just adds up the smaller tokens and replaces them with the larger values when the other people are taking their turns.

And we may not use the modifiers like "immune to damage" or "all damage: melee" as much, but those damage dealt/taken +/- tokens are a huge help.

With first edition i got knitting counters for characters and used a bunch of 6 sided dice for other cards.

With EE I've gone totally over to the HP tokens...I love em.  I haven't used the modifier tokens much.  I like the concept but either forget or there isn't one that marks just what I want.

Someone above mentioned wanting for of some tokens for effects that spread over many targets.  I keep thinking it would be useful to have a card (preferably oversized) that has world modifer boxes.  So when a card turns all damage into melee you put the all damage melee token in the universal (or some name) box. When all villain targets do damage +1 you put that in the villain targets box. When something reduces damage done by all non-villain targets you put a damage -1 in the hero and environment boxes.

Example sections:

Universal

Hero Targets

Villain Targets

Environment Targets

It seems like it would save on token needs and be a quick reference.  Just a thought, haven't tried it in practice.
